1. Exemption allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. The application stands disposed of.

The petitioners, vide the present petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India read with Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, seek quashing of FIR No.084/2021 dated 07.03.2021 registered under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC at P.S. Hari Nagar, Delhi and all proceedings emanating therefrom in view of the Settlement Deed dated 19.08.2021 arrived at between the parties.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 16/12/2023 at 00:54:10 4.

This petition is accompanied by the Settlement Deed dated 19.08.2021 [Annexure-P-2] and is also supported by affidavits of all the petitioners and of respondent no.2, alongwith proofs of their respective I.Ds.
5. Petitioner nos.1 to 4 as also respondent no.2 are present in Court and have been identified by the IO.
Their credentials have been verified by this Court.

sentences.text: Issue Notice.
7. Learned ASC for State accepts notice.
She confirms that since the present FIR has arisen out of matrimonial disputes, she has no objection to the quashing of the said FIR.
8. Respondent no.2 confirms that the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have been granted divorce by mutual consent vide Decree of Divorce dated 27.10.2023.

She further affirms the Settlement Deed dated 19.08.2021 whereby the petitioner no.1 has already paid her a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- and the remaining amount of Rs.5,00,000/- has been handed over to the respondent no.2 vide DD no.382560 issued on 13.12.2023 drawn on Canara Bank in full and final settlement of all her claims including alimony, maintenance (present, past and future), stridhan etc.

She states that he has no objection to the quashing of the present FIR.
9.

In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. Vs. Babita Raguvanshi & Anr (2013) 4 SCC 58, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2012) 10 SCC 303 and Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2014) 6 SCC 466, this Court is This is a digitally signed order.
